ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A sprinkler fountain is in the shape of a semi-sphere that spews out water from all angles at a uniform speed $v$ such that without the presence of wind, the wetted region around the fountain forms a circle in the $X Y$ plane with the fountain centered on it.
Now suppose there is a constant wind blowing in a direction parallel to the ground such that the force acting on each water molecule is proportional to their weight. The wetted region forms the shape below where the fountain is placed at $(0,0)$. Determine the exit speed of water $v$ in meters per second. Round to two significant digits. All dimensions are in meters.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an XY plane with a coordinate grid, the light blue region indicates the region wetted by water, and the black dot is marked at the origin (0,0). The light blue region is obviously asymmetric in the horizontal direction relative to the black dot, extending more to the left than to the right, so the displacement caused by the wind is along the horizontal x direction. Observing the vertical direction, the blue region reaches approximately y=+0.64 m at the highest and approximately y=-0.64 m at the lowest, so the half-width perpendicular to the wind direction is about R=0.64 m. Reasoning: The force of the wind is parallel to the ground and along the x direction, so it only changes the motion in the x direction, does not change the motion in the y direction, and also does not change the flight time in the vertical direction. The flight time of the water drop in the vertical direction is still determined by the initial vertical velocity and gravity; the displacement in the y direction is determined only by the initial y-direction velocity multiplied by the flight time. Therefore, the maximum range perpendicular to the wind direction remains the maximum horizontal range R=v^2/g of an ordinary projectile when there is no wind. Reading from the figure gives R≈0.64 m, so v=sqrt(gR)=sqrt(9.8×0.64)=sqrt(6.272)≈2.50 m/s. To two significant figures, v≈2.5 m/s.

method.method_draft: Use the footprint width perpendicular to the wind as an invariant range. First read the diagram: the blue wetted region is horizontally asymmetric about the black dot at (0,0), so the wind direction is along the horizontal x-axis; the vertical extent is about y=+0.64 m to y=-0.64 m, giving a transverse semi-width R≈0.64 m. From the text, water exits in all upward directions with common speed v, while the wind force is horizontal. Because the wind has no vertical-in-plane y component, the y-displacement of any drop is governed only by its initial transverse velocity and the time of flight, and the time of flight is governed only by the vertical component and gravity. The maximum transverse ground range over all launch angles is therefore the ordinary projectile maximum range R=v^2/g. Solve v=sqrt(gR)≈sqrt(9.8·0.64)≈2.5 m/s, then round to two significant digits.

推理：风的力平行于地面且沿x方向，因此它只改变x方向运动，不改变y方向运动，也不改变竖直方向的飞行时间。水滴竖直方向的飞行时间仍由初始竖直速度和重力决定；y方向位移只由初始y方向速度乘以飞行时间决定。因此，垂直于风向的最大射程保持为无风时普通抛体的最大水平射程R=v^2/g。由图读出R≈0.64 m，所以v=sqrt(gR)=sqrt(9.8×0.64)=sqrt(6.272)≈2.50 m/s。按两位有效数字，v≈2.5 m/s。

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A sprinkler fountain is in the shape of a semi-sphere that spews out water from all angles at a uniform speed $v$ such that, without the presence of wind, the wetted region around the fountain forms a circle in the $XY$ plane with the fountain centered on it. Now suppose there is a constant wind blowing in a direction parallel to the ground such that the force acting on each water molecule is proportional to their weight. The wetted region forms the shape shown, where the fountain is placed at $(0,0)$. Determine the exit speed of water $v$ in meters per second. Round to two significant digits. All dimensions are in meters.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is an XY plane with a coordinate grid, the light blue region indicates the region wetted by water, and the black dot is marked at the origin (0,0). The light blue region is obviously asymmetric in the horizontal direction relative to the black dot, extending more to the left than to the right, so the displacement caused by the wind is along the horizontal x direction. Observing the vertical direction, the blue region reaches approximately y=+0.64 m at the highest and approximately y=-0.64 m at the lowest, so the half-width perpendicular to the wind direction is about R=0.64 m.

Reasoning: The force of the wind is parallel to the ground and along the x direction, so it only changes the motion in the x direction, does not change the motion in the y direction, and also does not change the flight time in the vertical direction. The flight time of the water drop in the vertical direction is still determined by the initial vertical velocity and gravity; the displacement in the y direction is determined only by the initial y-direction velocity multiplied by the flight time. Therefore, the maximum range perpendicular to the wind direction remains the maximum horizontal range R=v^2/g of an ordinary projectile when there is no wind. Reading from the figure gives R≈0.64 m, so v=sqrt(gR)=sqrt(9.8×0.64)=sqrt(6.272)≈2.50 m/s. To two significant figures, v≈2.5 m/s.
